To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the α4 subunit is the most common subunit in GABAA receptors and the β1 subunits are widely recognised for their importance in receptor assembly but less is known of their influence on extrasynapic GABAA receptor functions.
the pharmacological profile of α4βδ GABAA receptor differs from that of α4β2 GABAA receptor, and is similar to that of α4δ GABAA and α4β2δ receptors.
we have characterised a novel GABAA receptor sub-unit isoform, which is sensitive to the β-selective inhibitor salicilylidine salicyhydrazide and the neurosteroid tetrahdrodeoxycorticosterone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pharmacology of a novel receptor isoform that may be of importance to the understanding of the function of GABAA receptors in the central nervous system.
the molecular pharmacology and physiology of GABAA receptors.
the pharmacological and molecular properties of the α4βδ GABAA receptor and its role as an extrasnaptic GABAA subtype in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pharmacological properties reported in this study are consistent with a role for α4βδ GABA receptors in the nervous system, particularly in the hippocampus and cortex, where the α4 subunit has been shown to be expressed.
the pharmacological properties described for human α4β2 GABAA receptors do not fully apply to the murine α4 subunit containing GABAA receptor isoforms.
the pharmacology of the murine α4 β1δ receptor has been characterised for the first time, but that the human isoform remains to be fully characterised.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
α4β1 and α4β2 receptors are likely to be the major GABAA receptor isoforms in the brain, and α4β3 and α4β4 receptors may play a minor role.

we provide the first pharmacological data for a potentially native extrasyncytic GABAA receptor, and that this data may be useful to those interested in the pharmacology and physiology of this receptor isoforms.
we have characterised a novel GABAA receptor isoform, and have demonstrated that the β1 subunits may play an important role in extrasynaptic GABA signalling.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the α4 subunit is not a sufficient indicator of a receptor’s pharmacological properties, and that the β1 sub-unit is a key determinant of the receptor’s pharmacology, and may be a key determinant of its role in the nervous system.
the β1 subunits are not only important for receptor assembly, trafficking or modulation but also for the pharmacology and function of the GABAARs.
the β1 sub-unit is not a simple ‘silent’ subunit in the GABAA receptor.
